depth_targets.title: Recommendations history
limitations: Vyomi logs applied IAM policy changes (grants and removals) here; it does not run GCP's IAM Recommender to generate new suggestions on its own, so nothing appears until you grant or remove access.

depth_targets.title: Service account keys
limitations: Key creation, listing and deletion are real and stateful, but the private key material is synthetic — it cannot be used to authenticate against anything outside Vyomi.

depth_targets.title: Service account Metrics tab
limitations: Per-service-account request metrics aren't modeled; Vyomi has no telemetry pipeline backing this view.

depth_targets.title: Service account Logs tab
limitations: Shows the admin-activity events Vyomi itself records for this service account — key create/delete, enable/disable, display-name updates, and Principals-with-access grants/revokes — not GCP's full Cloud Audit Log trail (e.g. API calls made using the account's own credentials).

depth_targets.title: Data Access audit logs configuration
limitations: Admin Read / Data Read / Data Write toggles and exempted principals are stored and returned exactly as configured, but Vyomi does not gate or emit audit log entries based on them.

depth_targets.title: Organization policy constraints
limitations: Policy constraints (predefined or custom) are created, listed and deleted for real, but Vyomi does not enforce them — a call that would violate a constraint in real GCP still succeeds here.

depth_targets.title: PAM Audit Logs
limitations: Shows the grant lifecycle events (requested, approved, denied, activated, expired, revoked) Vyomi's PAM core records; it does not aggregate the full Cloud Audit Log trail for entitlement changes made outside PAM.

depth_targets.title: PAM Settings
limitations: Notification channels and default approval settings aren't modeled.

depth_targets.title: Policy Analyzer
limitations: Queries who has a given role on the project from the stored IAM policy. Vyomi does not run full Cloud Asset Inventory analysis (inherited org/folder policy, resource-level IAM across products).

depth_targets.title: Workload Identity Federation — pool creation
limitations: Creating and listing a workload identity pool is real and stateful. Connecting an external OIDC/SAML identity provider and exchanging its tokens for Google credentials is not modeled.

depth_targets.title: Workforce Identity Federation
limitations: This feature requires an organization; Vyomi's GCP lens is project-scoped.

depth_targets.title: Groups
limitations: This feature requires an organization; Vyomi's GCP lens is project-scoped.

depth_targets.title: Principal Access Boundary
limitations: This feature requires an organization; Vyomi's GCP lens is project-scoped.

depth_targets.title: Managed Workload Identities
limitations: Managed Workload Identities auto-issues and rotates short-lived workload certificates (SPIFFE/mTLS trust domains) outside the key-file model; Vyomi doesn't run a certificate authority or credential-issuance pipeline to back that.

depth_targets.title: Asset Inventory
limitations: Cloud Asset Inventory's resource/IAM/org-policy search index isn't modeled.

depth_targets.title: Security Insights
limitations: IAM lint/insight analysis isn't modeled.

depth_targets.title: Quotas & System Limits
limitations: Shows real current usage (service accounts, their keys, custom roles, workload identity pools, organization policy constraints) against GCP's documented default per-project limits. Request-rate quotas (e.g. IAM API requests per minute) aren't shown — Vyomi doesn't meter API traffic — and limits are reference values only: Vyomi does not enforce them, so creating past a shown limit still succeeds.

depth_targets.title: Identity & Organization
limitations: This feature requires an organization; Vyomi's GCP lens is project-scoped.

depth_targets.title: Privacy & Security
limitations: This feature requires an organization; Vyomi's GCP lens is project-scoped.

depth_targets.title: Identity-Aware Proxy
limitations: IAP's per-resource access proxy isn't modeled.
